# Probing Non-Standard Neutrino Interactions with Supernova Neutrinos

Non-standard neutrino interactions (NSI) represent a compelling extension beyond the Standard Model, and they can be effectively probed by detecting the neutrino signal from a future galactic supernova. Of particular interest are the NSI-induced resonant conversions that take place in the deleptonised inner layers of the supernova, where the extreme matter conditions provide a unique environment for these interactions to manifest. These inner regions, characterized by their reduced electron content, offer a distinctive setting in which the effects of NSI on neutrino flavor evolution can become especially pronounced.

## Theoretical Framework

To capture these phenomena accurately, the study is conducted within a complete three-neutrino framework. This approach systematically accounts for the ways in which NSI modify neutrino propagation as the neutrinos traverse the supernova envelope. By incorporating the full three-flavor structure, the analysis is able to describe both the standard matter effects and the additional contributions arising from non-standard interactions, thereby providing a realistic picture of how the neutrino signal is shaped during its passage through the stellar medium.

## Detection Signatures in a Megaton Detector

The imprint of NSI could be observed in a Megaton-scale water Cherenkov detector through several distinct signatures. First, modulation effects in the $\bar\nu_e$ spectrum, induced by the passage of the shock wave through the supernova envelope, can carry information about non-standard interactions. Second, the time dependence of the electron fraction throughout the explosion provides an additional handle on NSI effects, as it governs the matter potential experienced by the propagating neutrinos. Third, Earth matter effects—arising when the neutrinos cross a portion of the Earth before reaching the detector—offer a further channel through which the influence of NSI can be discerned.

## The Neutronization Burst

Beyond these spectral and temporal features, the detectability of the neutronization $\nu_e$ burst offers an additional and independent means of identifying NSI effects. This early, sharply-timed burst of electron neutrinos is sensitive to the flavor conversion mechanisms operating in the supernova, and its observation could therefore serve as a valuable diagnostic tool for distinguishing standard from non-standard scenarios.

## Characteristic Spectral Features and Sensitivity

Perhaps most strikingly, the $\bar\nu_e$ spectrum can display dramatic features that originate from the internal NSI-induced resonant conversion. These features emerge for relatively modest values of the non-standard couplings: non-universal NSI strengths of only a few percent, and flavor-changing NSI strengths above a few $\times 10^{-5}$. The fact that such small couplings can produce observable effects highlights the remarkable sensitivity of supernova neutrino observations to non-standard interactions, making a future galactic supernova a powerful laboratory for exploring physics beyond the Standard Model.

# Probing Non-Standard Neutrino Interactions with Supernova Neutrinos

## Introduction

The detection of neutrinos from the historic supernova SN 1987A opened a new window into both stellar astrophysics and neutrino physics. A future galactic core-collapse supernova promises an unprecedented opportunity to study neutrino properties under extreme conditions that cannot be replicated in terrestrial laboratories. In this work, researchers investigate whether non-standard neutrino interactions (NSI)—hypothetical interactions beyond those described by the Standard Model of particle physics—can be probed through the detection of neutrinos emitted during such an event.

## Theoretical Framework

The study employs a complete three-neutrino framework that incorporates NSI-induced resonant conversions occurring within the dense stellar environment. As neutrinos propagate outward through the collapsing star, they traverse regions of varying matter density. In the presence of NSI, additional matter-induced potentials modify the effective Hamiltonian governing neutrino flavor evolution. These modifications can generate new resonant conversion points—analogous to the standard Mikheyev-Smirnov-Wolfenstein (MSW) resonances—that dramatically alter the flavor composition of the emerging neutrino flux.

NSI are typically parameterized by two distinct types of couplings: non-universal (NU) interactions, which affect diagonal elements of the neutrino potential and describe differences in the interaction strengths of different flavors, and flavor-changing (FC) interactions, which introduce off-diagonal couplings that directly mix neutrino flavors during propagation.

## Detection Strategy

The researchers examine how these effects would manifest in a next-generation Megaton-scale water Cherenkov detector. Two complementary detection signatures are considered. The first is the spectral modulation of the neutrino energy distribution, wherein NSI-induced conversions imprint characteristic distortions on the observed energy spectrum. The second is the neutronization burst—the brief, intense pulse of electron neutrinos released when the shock wave breaks through the neutrinosphere during the earliest moments of core collapse. This burst provides a particularly clean probe of flavor conversion effects due to its well-understood initial composition.

## Results

The central finding of the study is that the antineutrino spectrum can exhibit dramatic and observable features arising from internal NSI-induced resonant conversion. These signatures become prominent for non-universal NSI strengths at the level of just a few percent of the standard weak interaction strength, and for flavor-changing NSI couplings exceeding a few × 10⁻⁵. Such sensitivity levels are remarkable, as they probe interaction strengths that are extremely small and, in the case of the flavor-changing parameters, well beyond the reach of current laboratory experiments.

## Conclusion

These results demonstrate the significant potential of supernova neutrinos to serve as sensitive probes of new physics in the neutrino sector. Should a galactic supernova occur during the operational lifetime of a Megaton-class detector, the detailed structure of the observed neutrino and antineutrino spectra could reveal—or place stringent constraints upon—the existence of non-standard neutrino interactions, thereby complementing terrestrial searches and deepening our understanding of physics beyond the Standard Model.

# Probing Non-Standard Interactions with Megaton-Scale Cherenkov Detectors

## Introduction

The study of neutrino physics has entered a precision era, opening new avenues to search for phenomena beyond the Standard Model. Among the most compelling of these are **Non-Standard Interactions (NSI)**, which describe hypothetical couplings between neutrinos and matter that go beyond the well-established weak interactions. Detecting or constraining such interactions requires enormous detectors capable of capturing rare neutrino events with high statistical precision—a role uniquely suited to **megaton-scale water Cherenkov detectors**.

## Non-Standard Interactions (NSI)

Non-Standard Interactions arise naturally in many extensions of the Standard Model, including theories with new heavy mediators or additional gauge bosons. In the context of neutrino oscillations, NSI can be classified into two categories:

- **Charged-current (CC) NSI**, affecting neutrino production and detection.
- **Neutral-current (NC) NSI**, modifying neutrino propagation through matter via the coherent forward-scattering potential.

The presence of NSI would subtly alter the expected oscillation probabilities, introducing degeneracies with standard oscillation parameters such as the mixing angles and mass-squared differences. Disentangling these effects demands both high-statistics data and a broad range of neutrino energies and baselines.

## Megaton-Scale Detectors

To reach the sensitivities required, next-generation experiments are pushing detector volumes to the **megaton scale**. Facilities such as **Hyper-Kamiokande** represent a leap forward, containing hundreds of thousands of tons of ultra-pure water instrumented with tens of thousands of photomultiplier tubes.

The vast fiducial mass provides several key advantages:
- **Enhanced event rates** for atmospheric, solar, and accelerator-produced neutrinos.
- **Improved statistical power** to resolve fine features in oscillation spectra.
- **Access to rare processes**, including potential signatures of NSI-modified matter effects.

## The Cherenkov Technique

At the heart of these detectors lies the **Cherenkov effect**. When a charged particle—such as an electron or muon produced in a neutrino interaction—travels through water faster than the local speed of light in that medium, it emits a cone of faint blue light known as **Cherenkov radiation**.

By reconstructing the Cherenkov ring patterns, physicists can determine:
- The **direction** and **energy** of the incoming neutrino.
- The **flavor** of the interaction (distinguishing muon-like from electron-like events).
- The **event topology**, crucial for background rejection.

This imaging capability makes water Cherenkov detectors exceptionally well-suited for oscillation and NSI studies across a wide energy range.

## Synergy and Outlook

Combining megaton-scale volumes with the mature Cherenkov detection technique creates a powerful platform for exploring physics beyond the Standard Model. By precisely measuring neutrino oscillations over long baselines and across the full atmospheric neutrino spectrum, these experiments can place stringent constraints on NSI parameters—or potentially uncover the first hints of new interactions.

As the neutrino community advances toward these ambitious facilities, the interplay between **NSI theory**, **megaton detector technology**, and **Cherenkov imaging** will remain central to the quest for a deeper understanding of the fundamental laws of nature.

# Abstract

The next galactic core-collapse supernova offers a unique opportunity to probe neutrino properties under extreme astrophysical conditions inaccessible to terrestrial experiments. In this work, we investigate the sensitivity of a next-generation Megaton-scale water Cherenkov detector to non-standard neutrino interactions (NSI) using the neutrino signal from a galactic supernova at a fiducial distance of 10 kpc. Non-standard interactions modify the effective matter potential experienced by neutrinos as they propagate through the dense stellar envelope, altering flavor conversion probabilities and leaving imprints on the observed energy spectra and time evolution of the detected event rates. We perform detailed simulations of the inverse beta decay and elastic scattering channels, incorporating realistic supernova neutrino fluxes derived from hydrodynamical models, the Mikheyev-Smirnov-Wolfenstein (MSW) resonance structure, and collective oscillation effects. We demonstrate that both flavor-diagonal (ε_ee, ε_ττ) and flavor-changing (ε_eτ) NSI parameters can induce observable spectral distortions and modify the neutronization burst and accretion phase signatures. Accounting for statistical and systematic uncertainties, as well as degeneracies with astrophysical model parameters and the neutrino mass ordering, we find that a Megaton detector could constrain NSI couplings at the level of ε ≲ 10⁻²–10⁻¹, competitive with or exceeding current bounds from oscillation and scattering experiments in certain parameter regions. Our results highlight the complementarity of supernova neutrino observations with laboratory searches and underscore the potential of large-volume Cherenkov detectors to explore physics beyond the Standard Model in the neutrino sector.

---

*Keywords: non-standard neutrino interactions, supernova neutrinos, neutrino oscillations, water Cherenkov detector, physics beyond the Standard Model*

# Abstract

**Detectability of NSI-Induced Resonant Conversions in the Antineutrino Spectrum from a Future Galactic Supernova**

Non-standard neutrino interactions (NSI) can dramatically alter neutrino flavor evolution in the dense matter of a core-collapse supernova, potentially inducing novel resonant conversions absent in the standard three-flavor framework. In particular, non-universal and flavor-changing NSI can give rise to an "internal" or "I-resonance" occurring deep within the stellar envelope at densities where the standard MSW resonances do not operate. Here we investigate the observable imprints of such NSI-induced resonant conversions on the electron antineutrino spectrum emitted during the neutronization, accretion, and cooling phases of a future galactic supernova. Using representative supernova neutrino fluxes and a range of NSI parameters consistent with current terrestrial and astrophysical bounds, we compute the flavor-transformed spectra and propagate them to detection. We evaluate the sensitivity of next-generation large-volume detectors—including water Cherenkov (Hyper-Kamiokande), liquid scintillator (JUNO), and liquid argon (DUNE)—to the characteristic spectral distortions, including modifications to the average energy, spectral hardening, and the survival probability at the neutronization burst. We find that for NSI strengths of order $\varepsilon \gtrsim 10^{-2}$, the resulting swap features and altered high-energy tails in the $\bar{\nu}_e$ spectrum could be distinguishable from standard oscillation scenarios, particularly when time-dependent and energy-dependent signatures are combined across complementary detection channels. We further discuss the degeneracies between NSI effects, uncertainties in the neutrino mass ordering, collective oscillation effects, and the intrinsic supernova emission model, and assess the prospects for disentangling genuine new-physics signals from astrophysical modeling ambiguities. Our results highlight the potential of a high-statistics galactic supernova neutrino burst to probe NSI parameter space inaccessible to laboratory experiments, while underscoring the importance of multi-detector observations and improved theoretical modeling to achieve a robust discovery.

# Probing New Physics with Neutrinos from a Galactic Supernova

## Abstract

A galactic core-collapse supernova provides an unparalleled laboratory for testing neutrino properties and probing physics beyond the Standard Model. We investigate the sensitivity of next-generation neutrino detectors to non-standard neutrino interactions (NSI) using the anticipated neutrino signal from a supernova at a fiducial distance of 10 kpc. The intense flux of all neutrino flavors, emitted over the ~10 s deleptonization and cooling phases with characteristic energies of 10–20 MeV, traverses the steep matter density gradient of the stellar envelope, where NSI can significantly modify flavor conversion through modified Mikheyev-Smirnov-Wolfenstein (MSW) resonances.

We perform a combined analysis of the detected event spectra in liquid argon (DUNE), water Cherenkov (Hyper-Kamiokande), and liquid scintillator (JUNO) detectors, which offer complementary sensitivity to the $\nu_e$, $\bar{\nu}_e$, and neutral-current channels. By analyzing the spectral distortions, neutronization-burst suppression, and Earth-matter regeneration effects, we derive projected bounds on both non-universal and flavor-changing NSI parameters.

Assuming a standard neutrino mass ordering, we find that a galactic supernova can constrain the non-universal parameters to $|\varepsilon_{ee} - \varepsilon_{\mu\mu}| \lesssim 3 \times 10^{-2}$ and $|\varepsilon_{\tau\tau} - \varepsilon_{\mu\mu}| \lesssim 5 \times 10^{-2}$ (90% C.L.), while the flavor-changing couplings are bounded at $|\varepsilon_{e\mu}| \lesssim 2 \times 10^{-2}$, $|\varepsilon_{e\tau}| \lesssim 1 \times 10^{-2}$, and $|\varepsilon_{\mu\tau}| \lesssim 4 \times 10^{-2}$, all normalized to the coherent forward-scattering amplitude on d-quarks. These limits improve upon current terrestrial oscillation constraints on the $\varepsilon_{e\tau}$ sector by up to an order of magnitude, owing to the high densities probed within the progenitor. We further demonstrate that degeneracies between NSI parameters and astrophysical uncertainties in the initial flux spectra can be partially resolved through the time evolution of the signal and multi-channel detection. Our results underscore the discovery potential of the next galactic supernova as a probe of new neutrino interactions inaccessible to laboratory experiments.

---

*Keywords: supernova neutrinos, non-standard interactions, neutrino oscillations, MSW effect, physics beyond the Standard Model*

**Note:** The quantitative bounds presented above are illustrative values consistent with typical projections in the literature. For a specific publication, these should be recomputed with a dedicated statistical analysis using current best-fit oscillation parameters and detailed detector response functions.
